**Herlev og Gentofte Hospital** is a major healthcare organization and hospital located in [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], Denmark. It is systematically tracked in national clinical quality databases, specifically the Akut Kirurgi Databasen (AKDB), which monitors the quality, safety, and outcomes of acute surgical care. Within the regional reporting structure, the hospital's data contributes to the aggregate figures for [[hovedstaden-region-i-alt|Hovedstaden Region i alt]].

The hospital's performance is evaluated across multiple clinical quality indicators. For [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], which measures the proportion of patients receiving antibiotic treatment within three hours, Herlev og Gentofte Hospital reported a compliance rate of 26.9% (81 out of 301 patients) for the period from September 1, 2022, to August 31, 2023 [^src1]. In the subsequent reporting period (September 1, 2023, to August 31, 2024), this figure slightly increased to 27.3% (84 out of 308 patients) [^src7]. 

Regarding the supplementary [[indikator-5x|Indikator 5x]], which tracks the speed of surgical intervention for life-threatening conditions such as perforation, ischemia, and bleeding, the hospital achieved a rate of 21.8% (19 out of 87 patients) during the 2022–2023 period [^src2]. In the 2023–2024 period, the hospital's performance on related metrics showed variations, with a reported 17.6% (54 out of 306) on another specific indicator [^src8]. The hospital is also evaluated on other process indicators, such as early nutritional assessment (Indicator 8) [^src3].

Patient demographics and comorbidities are closely monitored to adjust for risk and evaluate postoperative outcomes. An analysis of the patient composition for the 2022–2023 period revealed that out of 306 operated patients at the hospital, 19 (0.60%) had gastrointestinal cancer diseases and 4 (0.13%) had other cancer diseases [^src4]. Furthermore, when evaluating 30-day mortality after acute surgery among patients with light to moderate comorbidity—specifically those with a [[charlson-score-1-2|Charlson Score = 1 eller 2]]—the hospital recorded 13 deaths out of 117 patients, resulting in a mortality rate of 11.1% [^src5]. In the following year, this specific mortality metric was recorded at 11.8% (17 out of 144 patients) [^src9]. 

Broader demographic and mortality distributions, including age, gender, and higher comorbidity levels (Charlson Score ≥ 3), are also tracked to support clinical benchmarking and resource allocation [^src6] [^src10]. These comprehensive metrics are utilized by the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute and the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Program to drive continuous improvement in acute surgical care across the country.
